summary.intent: Release prep for michi 0.11: rewrite changesets so they are user-first, then upgrade to Callisto 0.22 (simplified TOML config) and check whether Rust and crate dependencies are current.
summary.outcome: Changesets were rewritten into 17 audience-split entries and pushed to stacked PRs #137/#138, with the changeset standard saved to memory. A Callisto 0.22 migration research agent was launched, with no config changes made yet. Rust was confirmed current on CI (stable 1.100.0), and both lockfiles were updated (24 workspace changes, 6 in fuzz) on a new branch and opened as a PR after MSRV, check and test runs.

repo: Changesets feed per-package changelogs via Callisto, which copies each entry into every listed package's changelog, so entries must be split by audience (Rust core, pipeline, JS) and use that audience's method names.

The repo has a `courier:changeset` skill that must be used for every changeset edit. Its rules: lead with reader impact, write old → new → action for breaking changes, omit implementation detail, and put fixes to unreleased behaviour into the feature's own entry.
michi tracks the `stable` Rust channel, so CI uses the latest Rust (1.100.0). The MSRV is 1.93, and the local machine had rustc 1.99.1.

michi was on Callisto 0.20.0. Migrating to 0.22 may affect the release workflow customizations (napi build matrix, macOS runner override, attestation signing, npm/crates.io tokens), renamed error codes, ignored npm scripts, the decision-file schema, and the open release PR #131.
`just check` includes a markdown format check, and `just test` includes the Node binding tests; wall-clock scaling tests are sensitive to machine load.
There is a separate fuzz lockfile that needs updating alongside the workspace lockfile.
Updated napi crates all require Rust 1.88 or older, within the 1.93 MSRV.
workflow: `cargo update --workspace` only updates the workspace's own crates, not their dependencies; run `cargo update` without that flag to preview real lockfile updates.
Use `cargo info` to look up the latest crate versions rather than hand-built HTTP requests to crates.io.
Never put the user's email in request headers such as User-Agent; a safety check blocked this once.
Passing CI and merged PRs do not mean a release is ready; audit the release artifacts (changelog rendering, docs, API freeze) from the reader's view.
Stack dependent PRs (#138 on #137) and retarget after the base merges.

friction: The user had to point out that the changesets were hard to read; the first pass only fixed factual errors and ignored the writing.
The `courier:changeset` skill was skipped, causing rework.
The pipeline patch changeset wrongly described bugs in unreleased code.
`just test` on the stacked #138 branch failed on wall-clock scaling tests with a machine load average of 151, so local results were unreliable and CI is the real check.
The first dependency check was wrong because `cargo update --workspace` reported nothing to update.
A crates.io lookup included the user's email in the User-Agent header and was blocked by the safety check; it was redone with `cargo info`.
The local rustc (1.99.1) is behind CI's 1.100.0.
open_items: Complete the Callisto 0.20 → 0.22 migration: new simplified `callisto.toml`, regenerated workflow, breaking-change handling, and the effect on open release PR #131. This is planned on a branch stacked after #137/#138.
Merge #137 first, then #138 retargets onto main; confirm CI passes the timing-sensitive tests.
22 direct dependencies are behind their latest major or incompatible versions and need manifest changes to adopt; none were upgraded.
Local Rust toolchain should be updated to match CI's 1.100.0.
